thesisQuality.basis: Strong band: signed hyperscale supply agreement plus 29% C&I growth and capacity/capability expansion demonstrate adoption; undisclosed customer economics cap the score below exceptional.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Strong band: Q2 sales +11%, C&I +29%, first-half net income $216M versus $118M; mixed residential trajectory and capital intensity prevent exceptional treatment.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Mixed/unproven band: market cap near $12.17B is roughly 48% above year-end 2025 while current evidence lacks a complete forward per-share valuation bridge; upside exists but asymmetry is not established.

catalystScore.basis: Strong band: signed hyperscale supply, rapidly increasing data-center backlog, capacity expansion and capability acquisitions provide multiple source-supported execution catalysts.

governancePower.basis: Mixed/adequate band: management is executing acquisitions and capacity investment alongside improving earnings, but the evidence set does not establish exceptional long-duration capital-allocation outcomes.

alignment2036.basis: Exceptional-band entry is supported by exposure to resilient power, data-center uptime, distributed generation and storage/control infrastructure across plausible long-duration electrification/compute futures.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Strong band: residential generation, C&I, data centers, telecom/rental, controls and storage reuse core power capabilities across several demand channels.

bottleneckControl.basis: Strong band: customer qualification, generator capacity, switchgear/enclosures and controls participate in constrained mission-critical power delivery, but Generac does not control the full grid/fuel bottleneck.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Strong band: portfolio spans standby generation, C&I, storage and controls, providing multiple paths across grid-resilience scenarios; residential cyclicality and architecture shifts remain material.

substitutionResilience.basis: Strong band: qualification and integrated generation/switchgear/storage/control capabilities create replacement friction, while batteries/grid services and alternative generation remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Mixed band: added domestic C&I capacity and acquired enclosure/switchgear capability improve control, but evidence does not demonstrate tested multi-source resilience across critical inputs.

pricingPower.basis: Strong-band lower range: C&I operating leverage and margin improvement support some economic capture, but tariff refunds contributed to margin gains and contract pricing/pass-through terms are undisclosed.

riskEvidence.basis: Moderate risk: customer/economic concentration is undisclosed, simultaneous capacity/acquisition execution is material, and architecture substitution remains credible; current operating conversion offsets but does not eliminate these risks.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current SEC financials and multiple primary operating sources provide strong factual coverage; confidence is reduced by issuer-heavy strategic evidence, undisclosed hyperscale economics and incomplete independent valuation corroboration.

scoreRecord.thesis: Generac is converting a historically generator-centric franchise into a broader mission-critical power platform as data-center demand, grid constraints and resilience needs expand, with current C&I growth providing operating confirmation.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Data-center customer economics and concentration remain undisclosed while capacity/acquisition investment and alternative power architectures can impair returns.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Conversion of hyperscale/data-center backlog into reported revenue, margins and cash flow through 2027.

scoreBreakdown.note: Earth score equals weighted component score less methodology risk penalty; data confidence is reported separately and remains above the publishable floor.
